2 findings carried by reviewers against `content/wiki/org/bytedance-seed.md`, batched into one job because they concern the same file. Each is stated below in the reviewing reviewer's own words. Fix every one, or say in `RESULT.md` which you did not and why — a finding you leave standing must keep its file.

### Declare byteplus.com in publishes_from once the field exists

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260906-01-carry-1.md`.

The brief required `publishes_from`; it cannot be declared today. `entrySchema` in `lib/schema.mjs` is `.strict()` and rejects the key — measured: `entrySchema.safeParse({...entry, publishes_from: ['bytedance.com']})` returns `Unrecognized key: "publishes_from"` — and `grep publishes_from lib/` returns no matches, because the field lives only in the pending `separate-a-claim-from-a-fact` amendment. The live substitute already covers part of the ground: `orgNameTokens` in `lib/render/frontier.mjs` derives the token `bytedance` from this entry's display name, so a claim cited from `seed.bytedance.com` attributes correctly with no declaration. What it does not cover is the domain this entry itself establishes as the only place the model can be called from abroad — `ai.byteplus.com`, whose registrable label `byteplus` is not one of the org's name tokens. When the field lands, this entry needs `publishes_from: [byteplus.com]`, or a real BytePlus-hosted Seed claim renders as the honest-looking blank FM-N6 describes.

### Reconsider the bare "Seed" alias — it widens two joins that ignore alias class

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260906-01-carry-2.md`.

The entry declares `- name: Seed / class: manual`. `manual` correctly keeps the linker off it, but neither mechanism that reads this list looks at `class`: `matchProviders` and `orgNameTokens` in `lib/render/frontier.mjs` both map `aliases[].name` with a 3-character floor and nothing else. So `seed` becomes (a) a board-join key that matches any future catalog provider id containing the substring — today only `bytedance-seed`, tomorrow anything a router files under a name with `seed` in it — and (b) an ownership token, making any registrable domain whose bought label is exactly `seed` read as this organisation's own. The alias buys nothing in return, since `manual` means it is never wrapped in prose. Dropping it, or narrowing it to a form that carries the vendor name, would close both without any loss.

### Correct the gpt-6-astra endpoint fact — two Azure endpoints, and the quoted name is truncated

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260906-09-carry-1.md`.

The fact `azure_serves_gpt_6_astra` reads `one endpoint named "Azure | openai/gpt-6-astra", tags `azure` and `azure/us``. Fetched https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models/openai/gpt-6-astra/endpoints on 2026-09-06: it returns 5 endpoints, of which TWO are Azure, and both are named `Azure | openai/gpt-6-astra-20260903` — one carrying tag `azure`, the other `azure/us`. So it is two endpoints with one tag each, not one endpoint with two tags, and the quoted name omits the `-20260903` suffix the API actually returns. The conclusion the fact supports is unaffected (Azure does serve this openai/ row, and the 123-row sweep it spot-checks reproduces exactly), so this is a transcription fix, not a retraction. This fact is not transcluded into the prose; it renders only in the Facts section.

### Several fact values are sentence fragments that only parse inside the prose

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260906-09-carry-2.md`.

`lib/render/entry.mjs:87` renders every fact in a standalone Facts section, independent of the body. Read there, some values are missing their subject because they were written to be dropped into a transcluding sentence: `only_dead_upstream_in_the_catalog` begins "the only one. 179 of the 431 rows…", `mai_rows_on_this_router` begins "none. Across all 431 rows…", and `wizardlm_router_description` ends with the editorial aside "— OpenRouter's own catalog copy, not Microsoft's". Rewriting these three values to stand alone (and moving the aside into the body, which already makes the same point) would leave the prose reading identically while making the Facts section legible on its own.

items.detail:
3 findings carried by reviewers against `content/wiki/org/nous-research.md`, batched into one job because they concern the same file. Each is stated below in the reviewing reviewer's own words. Fix every one, or say in `RESULT.md` which you did not and why — a finding you leave standing must keep its file.

### Cite the three comparison likes counts, or narrow the fact to the one the URL supports

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260906-03-carry-1.md`.

The fact `hermes_4_likes` carries "299, against 215 for Hermes-4-70B, 181 for Hermes-4-14B and 94 for Hermes-4-405B" with a single `source_url`, https://huggingface.co/api/models/NousResearch/Hermes-4.3-36B. That document contains only the 299. I fetched all four endpoints on 2026-09-06 and every number is right (Hermes-4.3-36B likes=299, Hermes-4-70B likes=215, Hermes-4-14B likes=181, Hermes-4-405B likes=94), so nothing is false — but a reader following the rendered link can check one figure in four, and the wiki spec requires a fact's source be reachable from the rendered page. Either split the comparison into per-model facts each citing its own `/api/models/...` endpoint, or reduce this fact to the 299 and move the comparison into prose that names the other three URLs.

### The portal row count does not reproduce at 332

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260906-03-carry-2.md`.

`portal_catalog` states "332 distinct named model rows, counted from the landing page's own per-1M price cells". Fetching https://portal.nousresearch.com/ on 2026-09-06 (the fact's own `accessed` date) and extracting the embedded `{"displayName","modelName","tokenPrice"}` rows gives 346 rows, 346 distinct `modelName`, 337 distinct `displayName`, and 333 distinct `modelName` once the 13 `~`-prefixed free-tier duplicate ids are dropped. No counting convention I tried lands on 332; the nearest is 333. Same-day drift of one row is the likely explanation and this is not blocking, but the figure should either be re-counted with the convention stated ("distinct model ids, free-tier duplicates excluded") or softened. The load-bearing half of the claim is exactly right and I confirmed it: of all 346 rows, zero match /nous|hermes|nomos|consilience|psyche/ in either id or display name.

### Two launch-post quotes are classed `slow` where `dated` is what they are

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260906-03-carry-3.md`.

`hermes_4_3_claim` ("nearly matches (and in some cases exceeds) the performance of Hermes 4 70B at half the parameter cost") and `psyche_production_first` ("our first production model post-trained entirely on the Psyche network") both carry `volatility: slow`, which the schema defines as re-check within 120 days. Both are fixed sentences in a dated launch post and cannot change; `dated` is the class the spec defines for exactly this ("true as of its date, displayed with the date, never re-checked"). As classed they will enter the overdue sweep in February for a re-check that can only confirm the same bytes. The neighbouring quote fact `psyche`, from the same kind of source, is already classed `dated`.

items.detail: 3 findings carried by reviewers against `content/wiki/org/poolside.md`, batched into one job because they concern the same file. Each is stated below in the reviewing reviewer's own words. Fix every one, or say in `RESULT.md` which you did not and why — a finding you leave standing must keep its file. ### "Not one of the eight rivals is in that class" overreaches — three publish no size Carried in `data/carried/j-20260906-05-carry-1.md`. The body asserts "Not one of the eight rivals in its own comparison table is in that class". The entry's own transcluded `comparison_table_sizes`, rendered in the next breath, says five rivals publish a size (Tencent Hy3 295B-A21B, Nemotron 3 Ultra 550B-A55B, Inkling 975B-A41B, DeepSeek-V4-Pro Max 1.6T-A49B, Kimi K3 2.8T-A50B) "and Qwen 3.7 Max, Muse Spark 1.1 and Claude Fable 5 carrying an em dash where a size would go". For those three the size is undisclosed, not known-to-be-larger, so the sentence claims more than the table shows. "Not one of the five that publishes a size is in that class, and three publish none" is exact and no weaker. Carried rather than blocked because the transclusion immediately below discloses the em dashes, so the reader can see the gap. Re-filed from the pass-1 record, confirmed here against the entry's own front matter. ### Restore the vendor's hedge to the weight-class quote Carried in `data/carried/j-20260906-05-carry-2.md`. `weight_class_claim` quotes "the most capable agentic coding model in its weight class by a wide margin" and labels it "the vendor's own bolded comparison", which is honest and not a misquotation. But the served sentence is "Laguna S 2.1 is, as far as we can measure, the most capable agentic coding model in its weight class by a wide margin." — confirmed by fetching https://poolside.ai/blog/introducing-laguna-s-2-1 on 2026-09-06 (HTTP 200, 465,772 bytes) and finding "as far as we can measure" twice, once in the rendered HTML and once in the Sanity block payload as a span reading "Laguna S 2.1 is, as far as we can measure, ". Dropping that clause makes Poolside sound more absolute than it was, in a paragraph whose whole argument is about the vendor's hedging. Adding it to the fact value costs nothing. Re-filed from the pass-1 record, confirmed here by my own fetch. ### Say "repository" on the two bare parenthetical dates in the licence paragraph Carried in `data/carried/j-20260906-05-carry-4.md`. The licence paragraph establishes a repository-creation frame ("Laguna XS.2's repository went up on 23 April 2026 ... Laguna M.1's on 15 June") and then drops the noun for the next two: "Laguna XS 2.1 (20 June) is openmdw-1.1 and Laguna S 2.1 (13 July) is ...". Both parentheticals are Hugging Face createdAt dates and both are correct, but a reader landing mid-paragraph reads them as release dates, and the announcements were 2 July and 21 July — dates the entry's own timeline carries three rows apart from these. Not a false claim; a dropped qualifier on a number the entry states twice under two different meanings. "XS 2.1's repository (20 June)" would close it. ### Retiring these findings These files' presence is what puts the findings in the Pulse's derived queue. Delete the file for each finding you fixed, in the same diff as the fix — that is what removes the item, and a file left in place puts the same finding back on the next Pulse run: - `data/carried/j-20260906-05-carry-1.md` - `data/carried/j-20260906-05-carry-2.md` - `data/carried/j-20260906-05-carry-4.md`

`data/proposals/link-node-modules-before-the-author-runs.md` (added by this diff, 2026-09-07) proposes what `data/proposals/author-worktrees-carry-no-node-modules.md` (2026-09-04, still standing in the tree) already proposes: "Link `node_modules` into a job worktree when the worktree is created, not only inside `runGates`." The slugs differ, so nothing auto-discards, and both are selectable. The new file is not redundant in every part — it adds that `linkNodeModules` is already idempotent, so the gate-time call needs no change, and it names the exact insertion point — while the older one carries a second half the new one drops: teaching `unlinkNodeModules` to tell a junction it created from a real directory a job installed, rather than calling `unlinkSync` on a directory and swallowing the throw. Whoever takes this should work from one file holding both halves and drop the other, rather than let two proposals for one fix compete for selection. (The older file's line citation has also drifted: it names `loop/lib/gates.mjs:177` for the sole `linkNodeModules` call, which is `:300` today.)

The docket quotes the announcement as "Continuous Ranked Probability Score (CRPS) improvement of up to 60% against IMERG, 30% for MRMS, and 10% against rain gauge measurements". I fetched https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/google-deepmind/introducing-weathernext-3/ on 2026-09-07 and the same sentence ends "...and 10% against rain gauge measurements for early lead times". The docket's own done-when line already requires every accuracy figure to name whoever measured it and against what; the lead-time condition belongs in that list, because a CRPS gain at early lead times is not a medium-range claim. Fix: carry the four words.

The conclusion the passage reaches — assign no `agents` domain, because `lib/domains.mjs` forbids inference — is unaffected and is if anything stronger. The fix is one word: name the single post that carries the phrase instead of "both Astra posts".
